title: Songket gold weaving
summary: Songket is a hand-woven cloth of the Malay world in which gold and silver threads are laid in between the ground threads on a loom, so that glittering shoots, flowers and stars rise row by row from a dark silk or cotton ground. The same motif is often turned around so the two ends of a long cloth answer each other.
howToPlay: Pick a thread colour and a woven shape from the tray under the cloth.
Tap a square to weave it: the same shape appears on the square turned half way round the cloth.
Copy the small cloth shown above, then press Check.
rules: The cloth is turned half way round on itself, as a long cloth with matching ends is.
A square counts only when its woven shape and its thread colour both match the target.
Three stars need a nearly perfect copy; you can undo or clear as often as you like.
heritageNote: Songket is woven in Malaysia, Brunei and Indonesia, notably in Terengganu, Kelantan, Palembang, the Minangkabau highlands, Bali and Lombok. Weavers learn within the family, and many motif names recall plants, such as the young bamboo shoot, the flower and the leaf.
